newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Public Bank announces bonus, right issues.
newsitem.headline: Public Bank announces bonus, right issues.

text.p: Malaysia's Public Bank Bhd has proposed bonus and rights issues to raise a total of 842 million ringgit ($339.5 million), a statement from the bank said on Wednesday.
A sale of 332,806,836 shares, at a par value of 0.50 ringgit each, has been planned under the bonus issue, the bank said in the statement to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE).

Under the rights issue, another 332,806,836 shares, priced at a par value of 0.50 ringgit each, has been proposed. These shares will be sold at 2.20 ringgit each if offered as local shares on the main board of the KLSE and at 3.30 ringgit each if quoted as "foreign shares", the statement said.

The two share exercises would raise a total of 842 million ringgit, the statement said, adding that 3.8 million will be written off for expenses and the balance 832.2 million will be utilised as working capital.
The two share exercises will result in Public Bank's paid-up capital swelling to 2.33 billion ringgit from 1.65 billion ringgit previously.

The proposals are not expected to have any significant effect on the earnings of the banking group for the year ending 31 December 1997, as they will only be concluded towards the end of the year, the statement said.
It said the exercises will, however, enhance the earnings of the group in future as the money raised will be used for expansion of operations.
